LESSON: CAPACIT Y

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: MATHEMATICS FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.4: CAPACIT Y
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers CAPACIT Y, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four MATHEMATICS FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How can you measure capacity in real life situations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on CAPACIT Y together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: as learners in groups make 1⁄2 litre containers from locally available materials through filling and

emptying the container with substances such as water or sand using a 1 litre container.

• Self-efficacy: as learners show confidence in measuring capacity of 1⁄2 litre and 1⁄4 litre containers.

Values

• Responsibility: as learners make 1⁄4 litre containers from locally available materials through filling and emptying the

container with substances such as water or sand using a 1 litre container.

Values:
• Responsibility: as learners make 1⁄4 litre containers from locally available materials through filling and emptying the

container with substances such as water or sand using a 1 litre container.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Safety: learners prepare 1⁄2 litre and 1⁄4 litre containers while observing precautionary measures.

• Environmental education: learners make 1⁄2 litre containers from locally available materials to enhance environmental

education.

Link to other subjects learning areas

The learner is able to relate practical activities involving measurement of liquids to properties of matter in Science and Technology.

Suggested Learning Resources:

● 1 litre containers, containers of different sizes, water, sand, soil, relevant digital devices
